import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

Cabinets are a good idea, but with one change: keep the catalogs in the Markdown and have the card hide them when it draws, rather than removing them. Done that way, the whole feature lives in bob-plugins and almost no coordination with the four epics is needed. The report is at `research:202611/property_card_cabinets__cld.md` and is registered as an artifact. I only read code and the vault; nothing is built or tested.

**Why the catalogs have to stay in the file**
- Five things read the stored `[!areas]`, `[!projects]`, `[!notebooks]`, `[!albums]` and `[!records]` blocks:
  - bob's own SUBOPEN check;
  - the task-status-cycler plugin;
  - the album group-jump links;
  - capture's refusal to write into those sections;
  - mobile, git and agents.
- `decisions:notebook-routes-write-notes` already rejected an index that git, agents and mobile can't see.
- So each cabinet hides the bob-owned block at render time, the same way the card already hides the H1. It hides the `##` heading only when nothing else sits under it, so text you wrote is never hidden. Source mode and mobile still show the H2 sections.
- Each cabinet draws the stored block and decorates it with the existing catalog painters, so it shows exactly the same data. bob-cli doesn't change, nothing rides the release train, and Mac Capture is untouched.

**Coordination with qi, qj, qm and qp**
- Build the cabinets switched off behind their own preview setting. It must not be qm's `cardPreviewKinds`, which `qm.7` deletes.
- Restyle by changing the shared fold-row and Properties-row builders. Album Schema, bank Setup, qm's prose Outline and any qp fold row then become cabinets without anyone touching their code.
- The only gate is the final go-live phase. It waits for `qi.6`, `qm.7` and `qp.8` to close, because all three edit `glossary:property-card` and run screenshot reviews. qj has no overlap at all.
- None of the four epics needs a new phase or gate, and the cabinet work can start today.

**Changes I made to your requirements**
- **`q` also cancels**, alongside Esc and `Ctrl+[`. `decisions:q-and-ctrl-bracket-mirror-esc` requires this.
- **Hints in two places.** The digits light up on the cabinets themselves as well as in the status-bar footer. Your eyes are on the card when you press `_`; the footer covers the case where the card is scrolled away.
- **`__` picks cabinet 1, and `-` toggles Properties while picking.** Every album note will have Records and Schema, so `_` now opens the picker there. `__` keeps toggling Schema at one extra keystroke.
- **Fixed cabinet order:** Areas, Projects, Notebooks, Albums (or Records/Outline), then Schema/Setup, then Properties. It doesn't follow each note's heading order. This keeps `1` pointing at Schema or Setup.
- **Open/closed choices are remembered per note on each device.** Otherwise `sase.md`'s 64-line Projects cabinet would reopen every session.
- **Bank's widget stays named "Setup".** It shows accounts, categories and rules, not a schema.
- **Cards with no other cabinet keep `_` for their own details fold.** That covers records, notebooks, refs and leaf projects, and leaves qm's and qp's `_` designs alone.
- **Docs say "Properties cabinet" instead of "drawer"**, so "drawer" only means Task Drawer.

**One unverified risk:** I couldn't confirm from the code how Vim's `j`/`k` behaves over a long hidden block in the middle of a note. With the current title-hiding rule, landing on the block's edge would suddenly show all 106 raw lines of `eat.md`'s records. The report makes a quick real-Obsidian test the first step of the hiding phase.

The report also covers:
- the unified cabinet style;
- picker behavior and footer layout, with two diagrams;
- a draft `glossary:cabinet` entry and a proposed decision record;
- a 7-phase epic in which phases 2–5 run in parallel;
- four open questions, including whether the new cabinets start open or closed.
